content: The term diff refers to the difference between two versions of a page. This comparison can be accessed through the page history. In the page history, each version is accompanied by two radio buttons: the left column is used to select the older version, while the right column is used to select the newer version. By pressing the Compare selected versions button, the differences between the two selected versions are displayed. For specific cases, such as viewing the difference for a single edit or comparing an older version with the current version, you can click on cur or last in the page history or on the Recent Changes page. Additionally, during an edit conflict, the diff is shown to help you identify the exact changes that need to be reintegrated. The diff feature also works in preview mode, showing the differences between the currently stored version and the version being edited in the edit box. When viewing the diff, the two versions are displayed side by side. In left-to-right languages, the older version is shown on the left, while in right-to-left scripts, this arrangement is reversed. Paragraphs that differ are highlighted: yellow for the old version and green for the new version. Text removed within a paragraph is marked in red in the old version, while new text within a paragraph is marked in red in the new version. If an entire paragraph is removed or added, the text appears in black, and the corresponding side is left blank (white). Unchanged text is displayed in black on a grey background, with only the sections before and after the changed text shown. The diff highlights differences on a per-line basis. Some editors find that adding manual line breaks can improve the clarity of the diff function. The diff page also includes links to the user pages and talk pages of the editors who made the changes to the last and current versions. Links to the users' contribution lists are also provided. For sysops, a rollback button is available, allowing them to revert the page from the newer version to the older one. However, this rollback button is displayed even when viewing the diff between the most recent version of a page and an older version edited by a different user. In such cases, the rollback would not undo the specific change displayed in the diff. For example, if User A vandalized a page and User B partially reverted the vandalism, the diff would show the remaining vandalism, but rolling back would undo User B's partial repair. Edit summaries are also displayed on the diff page, appearing in the row beneath the usernames. If the user included links in their edit summary, these links are functional on the diff page. Additionally, the diff page provides links to both versions being compared, as well as to the previous and next diffs. The top of the diff page includes these links for easy navigation. When moving or copying a piece of text within a page or from another page, and simultaneously making other edits, it is helpful to separate these edits. This allows the diff function to be effectively used for reviewing the other changes. After the differences are displayed, the latest of the two compared versions is shown in full. In the Classic skin with a quickbar, the diff page does not include the quickbar, providing more space for viewing. This makes the diff page useful for viewing the page at full screen width without changing preferences. In the Monobook skin, the panels on the left are also present on the diff page. The page width may expand on a diff page due to the two-column layout and the presence of long URLs, which are not hidden. To compare two versions of a page using a URL, you can construct the URL as follows: Open the revision of one page you wish to compare, for example, `Diff&oldid=78722`, and the revision of the other page you wish to compare. Copy the `oldid` number of one page (e.g., `&oldid=78722` in the first example) and replace the text `oldid` with `diff` (e.g., `&diff=78722`). Paste this string into the URL of the other page between that page's title and its `oldid` (e.g., `&oldid=98420` in the second example). The resulting URL will compare the given versions of the two pages. You may remove the page title (e.g., `title=Main_Page` in the example above) from the URL if desired, but this is not necessary. To compare the current version of a page with a given `oldid`, you can use current after `diff=` instead of an `oldid`. For example, `Diff&diff=current&oldid=124558` would compare the current version of the page with the version that has `oldid=124558`.
